execution.description: Built `phase3 conditions`, which records a carbon.admission-conditions.v1 report's conditions as findings on a phase-3 root's own controller offline (no model, pod or RunPod key), idempotently, and prints the controller's identity; a write-once store id and CampaignController.identity(); and a committed designation of one admission controller per (Challenge, level) that check_lock and the CLI bind to.

expected: A finding consumed from a divergence report blocks LOCK of the affected level, and a LOCK cannot be checked against a controller that never consumed it.
observed: Each phase-3 root has its own controller and check_lock cross-checked whichever controller it was handed, so a LOCK checked against a fresh root would have bound an empty findings ledger: the W2 rule held per controller, not per level. Naming the authority needs an identity that survives reopening and never encodes a host path; the grant binding alone is shared by every root under one grant, so a write-once random store id was added beside it. The designated root is known only on the operator's host, so the committed designation is a fail-closed pending placeholder until the operator reports the identity. Re-consuming the same report bytes records nothing new, except that a finding repaired since is reopened, which is the controller's existing rule.
keep: A LOCK binds a designated controller by identity, never by path, and an undesignated, mismatched or pending designation refuses it.
Operator-side CLIs that only touch the ledger open the controller with a provider that cannot reach a model, a pod or a key.
Validate an external report completely before opening the store, and consume the exact bytes validated.
change: Admission state should live in a dedicated admission controller bound to a zero-spend grant, not inside an exhausted run root (recorded as a follow-up in GRAPHITE-ADMISSION-CONTROLLER-01).
Fill the battery Level 0 identity from the operator's `conditions --identity` on the R2 root in a one-line follow-up before any LOCK review.
